summary: Folded Wet Splash Sleeves V3 retains the solved V2 shoulder-to-elbow silhouette while replacing its smooth, glossy tube surface with a denser project-owned garment shell. Two non-repeating diagonal fold fields, localized cuff gather, a restrained underarm seam, elliptical cross-section, Cloth shading, ripstop texture detail, and live bounded wetness now give the visible splash-jacket overlay a less rigid presentation.

root_cause.v2_shape_problem: The retained V2 sleeve fixed the missing shoulder and uniform diameter, but its circular low-density surface and generic wet shader still read as a hard cyan tube.
root_cause.retained_shape: A twenty-eight-ring, thirty-six-sided surface preserves the broad deltoid and taper while adding bounded diagonal folds, cuff gathering, underarm seam relief, axial drape, and finite-difference surface normals.
root_cause.retained_material: The isolated opaque splash-jacket parent uses the three project-owned PFD ripstop texture channels at garment scale, Cloth shading, 0.72 dry roughness, bounded 0.44 saturated roughness, and the same presentation-only Wetness signal as the PFD.
root_cause.authority: Existing solved shoulders, elbows, body pose, paddle grip, collision, mass, rescue state, water, raft, and gameplay forces remain authoritative and unchanged.

renderer_evidence.technical_verdict: pass: guide and broadest-body front, profile, and rear captures retain the solved shoulder silhouette while showing visible surface folds, gathered cuff irregularity, and lower hard-plastic gloss than V2
renderer_evidence.photoreal_verdict: fail: the overlay remains procedural and synthetic, with exaggerated regular folds, abrupt torso/cuff integration, no skinned fabric compression, no identity-specific tailoring, and no production garment seam construction

validation.focused_material_authoring: isolated RaftSim.CreateSplashJacketMaterial command completed; saved material is opaque MSM_Cloth and uses exactly the three expected ripstop textures
validation.focused_python: 16/16 production-character and safety-gear source and review-lock contracts passed
validation.renderer_turntable: 5/5 identities captured with front, profile, and rear views

m5.result: 1/1 CrewAvatarPoseProduction passed renderer-enabled with 0 warnings and 0 errors

accepted: Both production shoulder sleeves now use denser folded garment topology instead of the retained smooth V2 tube surface.
All five roster identities meet the 1000-vertex mesh guard, live Cloth material-response guard, visible-shoulder contract, and existing shoulder-anchor contract.
The opaque splash-jacket parent uses the complete project-owned ripstop set and bounded live wetness without becoming gameplay authority.
The PFD still has no flotation shoulder pads; the folded geometry remains part of the splash-jacket layer.
No animation, mass, collision, raft, water, rescue, paddle-force, or gameplay-force authority changed.
rejected_or_open: The V2 smooth tapered sleeve presentation is superseded by this evidence set.
The retained procedural folds remain too regular and pronounced to pass as production cloth.
The torso, cuff, and underlying arm transitions still need a unified skinned garment with authored seams and compression deformation.
No named character-art reviewer or qualified whitewater guide has approved this evidence for release media.
open_gates: A named character-art reviewer must approve or replace the sleeve topology, torso integration, skinning, deformation, seams, tailoring, and wet-material response.
A qualified whitewater guide must approve shoulder range of motion and paddle-stroke biomechanics in motion.
M9 remains blocked by all wider human, platform, signing, media, clean-build, performance, and promotion gates.
